caption: R9 100 a month on a bakkie I need for work. Is that normal or am I paying for a lifestyle?

slides.title:
What my bakkie
really costs me
on R38 000 p/m
Living in Ceres
slides.body:
Male, 37
Married, one daughter (5)
Job: Packhouse manager, fruit
Household net income: R38 000 p/m

slides.title: Bakkie
slides.includes: Instalment R5 400, insurance R1 650, fuel R1 400, tyres & services R650
slides.body: I need it for orchard roads. I'd still rather it didn't cost more than our bond.

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: We bought before the rate hikes. I try not to look at the interest part.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers, farm stall, the odd box of fruit
slides.body: Fruit is free in season. I'm still spending R4 800, which says something.

slides.title: Daycare & school
slides.body: She started Grade R in January. The swimming lessons were her idea.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.includes: Saturday lunches, takeaways on night shift
slides.body: Peak season means I eat in the car. R2 300 and half of it is petrol-station pies.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, electricity, water, funeral policies, stokvel, phones, DStv, savings
slides.body: Medical aid is R3 600 of that. The rest are small things I never think about one at a time.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 000. It's what's left after the bakkie takes its share.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and its recurring expense detection showed the bakkie's costs in one place.

I'd never seen it as one number.

No bank login needed.
